sentences: **Most of the game's shaders are wave64: 23,841 of 26,503** (`fssm_header.wave_size()`: FSSM header flags word `u32[0xD4]` bit 5, `0x20` = wave32, `0` = wave64; 0 contradictions against GFX10 code-proven wave32/wave64 instructions across all 26,503 blobs): 10,974 of 12,101 PS, 9,282 of 9,282 mesh shaders, 2,236 of 2,236 VS, 1,154 of 2,689 CS and 195 of 195 GS, against 2,662 wave32 (1,535 CS and 1,127 PS).
A full-corpus translation at `ec8ec4c9` marks exactly these 23,841 `wave64` (`subgroup_size` 64) in the index.

Before the FSSM flag (#1900) the wave size came from code markers (64-bit EXEC/mask writes, `exec_hi`, `*_saveexec_b64`): at `6a6704df` they made 21,538 of the 26,487 shaders translated then wave64 (the figure quoted here was 21,545).
Against the flag they call 2,287 wave64 shaders wave32 (943 PS, 1,057 VS, 287 CS), whose code has no 64-bit EXEC/mask marker, and none the other way.
An older marker scan (`s_mov_b64 exec, -1`, `exec_hi`, `s_and/or_saveexec_b64` and 64-bit masks) counted 9,930 PS, 8,666 mesh shaders, 1,115 VS and 923 CS.
The translator maps a wave to a subgroup, and NVIDIA subgroups are 32 wide.

What that means: (1) lane-independent code, which is most pixel-shader math, is exact; (2) wave-wide branch decisions and reductions are made per 32-lane half, which is exact unless scalar state computed for one half is later consumed by the other; (3) lane indices from `v_mbcnt_lo/hi` and wave IDs from the merged-wave SGPR must be 64-lane values.
Mesh and compute shaders build thread IDs as wave_id·64 + mbcnt, so those need a mapping from `LocalInvocationIndex` (lane = index & 63, wave = index >> 6).

Full fidelity needs either 64-wide subgroups (AMD GPUs, via `VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control` requiredSubgroupSize = 64) or emulating cross-half ops (ballot, readlane, shuffles across halves) through workgroup memory.
